featured_reviews.review_text:
Victoria is an exceptional massage therapist. I had a 90-minute treatment with her last week, one which would be best described as “Thai Fusion”; it was mostly Thai technique, including the stretches, but with some long sweeping strokes that are reminiscent of Swedish style. (I had booked a Swedish massage, but, because of the effectiveness of her technique, classification didn’t matter to me in the end. Whatever it was, whatever we decide to call it, she did a great job.) Also worth noting: She is SO STRONG. She modulates her strength according to the client’s request, though, so you can certainly ask her to be soft. I asked for maximum pressure, and WOW; it was some deeeeeeeeep tissue work. I was a bit sore afterwards, but I fully expected that — and she had resolved several of my pain issues, so the lingering soreness was ABSOLUTELY worth it.

**I should add: If you are seeking pure Swedish style, this may not be the right place for you. I leave it in your hands to decide whether or not to give that a try; my experience was not great the first time, so I was offered a replacement session, and then I had the luck of being paired with Victoria for what was a non-Swedish-but-truly-therapeutic experience. (Thanks again, V!)

featured_reviews.name: Kashvi Ranwala
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was genuinely one of the worst spa experiences I’ve had.

First of all, zero professionalism — no uniforms, no sense of structure, nothing remotely “luxury.” Anyone calling this the best spa clearly does not know what they’re talking about. Save your money.

As soon as the lady entered (I wouldn’t go as far as calling her a therapist), she asked if I wanted the AC on. I said yes. She then said “it will be cold” and turned it off anyway.

When she started, I asked what oil she was using. Her answer was literally “massage oil.” When I asked which oil, she said “I don’t know.” That alone should tell you the level of training.

Then she made me get up mid-session to help move the bed, saying “help karo na move karne ko.” I paid ₹3000 — why am I rearranging furniture?

The technique was terrible. This was absolutely not deep tissue. I repeatedly asked for more pressure, and she kept insisting “this is only deep tissue” and then randomly asked if she should send a male therapist (why would you even suggest that when I’m clearly a woman who hasn’t asked for it?).

To make it worse, I could hear the receptionist watching TV loudly on his phone inside my treatment room. No ambience, no privacy.

I asked to stop the massage and requested a refund because the experience was unacceptable. They refused, claiming I had taken 30 minutes, which was false — she had only worked on the back of my legs and hadn’t even reached my back. At most it was 10–15 minutes. I then had to argue for a refund, with them trying to give me only ₹1500 back out of ₹3000. Finally, got 2000 back.

The most ridiculous part was when I explained I didn’t like the technique, and the receptionist actually said:
“How do you know what good deep tissue technique is?”

Unbelievable.

This place has no professionalism, no skill, and no respect for customers. Definitely not worth the money, and absolutely not a spa I would ever recommend.

featured_reviews.name: George Charalambous
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was the worst massage I have paid for.

Some of my reasons:
1. Location is hard to find and does not have a spa feel.
2. No questions were asked before the massage of any issues or problem areas
3. Massage tables do not have face holes - an issue if you have neck pain
4. No walkthrough on process including where to store clothing etc
5. My masseuse is not trained on any of the offered modalities. Having had training myself many years ago, I know what is expected. She was frustrated that I didn’t know the language.
6. A 60 minute massage ended after 40 minutes.
7. I was asked if I wanted “extra services” at the end of my massage…

I wouldn’t recommend this place to anyone unless they are looking for “extra services”.
